title: Lifting the divisor of a monomial-localization unit to a toric exponent
statement:
Let $P$ be a finitely generated integral saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and suppose it is sharp, meaning that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $n\geq0$ be an integer. For a coefficient ring $L$, write $L[P][t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ for the ring of finite sums of symbols $c z^q t^e$, with $q\in P$, $e\in\mathbf N^n$, $c\in L$, and multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$. If $L$ is local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_L$, let $B_L(P,n)$ be its completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] at $(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)$. Let $R$ be one of the following rings: (i) $B_k(P,n)$ for a field $k$; (ii) $B_C(P,n)/(\theta)$ for a Cohen ring $C$ of residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] and $\theta-p\in(z^q\ (q\neq0),t_1,\ldots,t_n)B_C(P,n)$. In case (ii), $p$ is prime and the residue field of $C$ is arbitrary of characteristic $p$. Write $z^q\in R$ for the chart monomials. Assume $R$ is a Noetherian normal domain [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] and all $z^q$ are nonzero. Identify $R$ with its image in $K=\operatorname{Frac}(R)$. Let $S=\{z^a:a\in P\}$ and let $\ell:R\to S^{-1}R$ be the localization homomorphism: fractions satisfy $f/s=g/t$ if $h(tf-sg)=0$ for some $h\in S$. For a height-one prime $\mathfrak q$ (a nonzero prime having no prime strictly between $(0)$ and itself), let $v_{\mathfrak q}:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ be the normalized additive valuation of the discrete valuation ring $R_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], with a uniformizer assigned value one. Use the affine principal divisor $\operatorname{div}_R(x)=\sum_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q=1}v_{\mathfrak q}(x)[\mathfrak q]$ in $\operatorname{Div}(R)$ [def-trf-affine-weil-divisor-class-group]. Then every $f\in R$ for which $\ell(f)$ is a unit is nonzero and admits an exponent $a_0\in P$ such that
$$v_{\mathfrak q}(f)=v_{\mathfrak q}(z^{a_0})\qquad\text{for every height-one prime }\mathfrak q\subset R,$$
or equivalently $\operatorname{div}_R(f)=\operatorname{div}_R(z^{a_0})$. The case $P=\{0\}$ is included, with $a_0=0$, as is $n=0$.

proof.text: Choose an inverse of $\ell(f)$, represented by $b/z^a$ with $b\in R$ and $a\in P$. The equality $fb/z^a=1/1$ means that $h(fb-z^a)=0$ for some $h\in S$. Every element of $S$ is nonzero, so cancellation in the domain gives $fb=z^a\ne0$. In particular $f\ne0$. This uses only the fraction equivalence relation in the statement.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-sharp-cone-lattice-intersection], identify $G$ with a lattice in $V=G\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\mathbf Q$ and $P=\sigma\cap G$, where $\sigma$ is its rational cone. All hypotheses are precisely the finite-generation, integrality, saturation and sharpness assumed for $P$. The half-space description in [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations] and the inequalities $\nu_F(g)=m_F\ge0$ give $g\in\sigma$. Hence $g$ is the image of an element $a_0\in P$, and $\nu_F(a_0)=m_F$ for all $F$.

proof.text: For $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak p_F$, the monomial valuation formula of [lem-trf-complete-toric-facet-valuations] gives $v_{\mathfrak q}(z^{a_0})=\nu_F(a_0)=m_F=v_{\mathfrak q}(f)$. At any other height-one prime, that node says $z^{a_0}\notin\mathfrak q$; its inverse $1/z^{a_0}$ belongs to $R_{\mathfrak q}$, so [lem-trf-normal-domain-principal-divisor-kernel] gives $v_{\mathfrak q}(z^{a_0})=0=v_{\mathfrak q}(f)$ by step 2. The pointwise equalities give equality of the finitely supported divisors. If $P=\{0\}$, its group completion is zero, the facet set is empty, step 1 reads $fb=1$, and we take $a_0=0$; the same valuation argument applies. For $n=0$ no step requires a parameter variable.
